reuse.why: The change extends getScheduledAmount, routes existing calculations and the API through it, and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold.

duplication.why: Repeated amount-resolution blocks are replaced with shared calls without introducing duplicate policy logic.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy stays in shared/schedules, tolerance stays in shared/rules, and API projection stays in api-models.

scope.why: The edits are focused on schedule amount policy, its consumers, API exposure, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralization simplifies ownership, although the optional string operator leaves the distinction between nominal and planned amounts implicit for existing amount-only callers.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers consistently call getScheduledAmount, which delegates tolerance calculation to getApproxNumberThreshold.

disguised_duplication.where: The former local amount calculations are removed and replaced with calls to the existing shared helper.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount gains the optional op parameter and an isapprox conditional; these directly represent the requested operator-dependent policy.
